description: A sincere, fan-made representation of Harry Potter's Wizarding World in Minecraft that still keeps the heart and feel of vanilla present.
body:
# A Wizarding World mod made by a true fan
You can show me a random picture or page out of the entire Harry Potter series, and I'll be able to tell you exactly which book it's from and what was happening at the time of the picture/page's events! So I will **not** produce a mod that I know does not line up with the series 👍🏻

# Keeps Minecraft the same
The mod practically has nothing now, but even when it does have some things... I won't create trolls or dragons or stuff that will essentially break the feel of Vanilla Minecraft. All the mod's additions will be homages to the Harry Potter series that can be utilised by a player in many different situations...

# Clear spellcasting mechanics
I don't like functional but impractical mods, who would stop and open their spellbook in the middle of an intense PvP fight? My spells are cast in one of two ways: right-clicking and left-clicking. That's **it.**
"How would the mod have more than two spells?", you may ask. I would answer: More wands!

# One OP Elder Wand per world
Although that's not implemented yet, the Elder Wand will require that its owner has the Dragon Egg, ensuring that only **one** Elder Wand circulates a Minecraft world!

title: Ava's Manhunt Starter
description:
Don't you hate how slow it is to start a manhunt recording?

Well fear not!  This solves that.
body:
# PLEASE NOTE!
## THIS IS NOT A COMPASS ADDON
**This datapack/mod is used ALONGSIDE compass addons etc!  Its purpose is to help make the preperation of recordings easier. Not just for the video's consistancy or the runner's sanity, but for the hunters too!**



<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/JUgOU7rw4tk" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

## YOU MUST DO THIS IN ORDER FOR THE DATAPACK TO WORK BEST!
**This is due to Mojang locking some datapack permissions behind server.properties!**


```
1. Open your server files
2. Head to "server.properties"
3. Set "function-permission-level=" to 3 or 4 AT LEAST!
4. Reset your server and then it's done!
```


# Command Functions!

* **/function manhunt:start_food**

This command does the following:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

```
Set all player spawnpoints to the executer's coordinates.
Clears all players, and then kills them.
Immediatly respawns all players. (does not enable doImmediateRespawn.)
Sets time to 250. (The best time for videos!)
Puts all players into survival mode.
Gives all players max saturation.
Reminds players to reset chat with F3 + D.
Clears weather.
Resets all advancements.
```

</details>



* **/function manhunt:start_nofood**

This command does the following:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

```
Same as manhunt:start_food, but does not give players saturation
This is helpful incase you feel like that is cheating, or bad for videos.
```

</details>



* **/function manhunt:pause**

This command does the following:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

```
Set the following player attributes to -1:
---------------
Attack Damage
Attack Speed
Interaction Range
Movement Speed
Jump Strength
---------------
Prevents players from losing air. (Does not use water breathing.)
Freezes the game with /tick freeze.
```

</details>



* **/function manhunt:pause_notick**

This command does the following:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

```
This does the exact same command as manhunt:pause, but does not use /tick freeze.
It is unrecommended to use this command, but if you have not enabled server permissions, it will be your only option.

Gives all mobs Slowness 255 + Resistance 255 + Weakness 255
Gives all players Resistance 255
```

</details>



* **/function manhunt:unpause**

This command does the following:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

```
Reverses the changes of manhunt:pause
```

</details>



* **/function manhunt:unpause_notick**

This command does the following:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

```
Reverses the changes of manhunt:pause_notick
(The reason this method is worse is due to it clearing Resistance from players, which may of been applied from an Enchanted Golden Apple, or something else.)
```

</details>

title: More Dyes
description: A minecraft mod aiming to infinitely* extend the range of available colored blocks.
body:
![Header](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/73a679b1468c854c4d28518fecbbbd93f0885b01.png)

# ⏫Update 1.1.0⏫
This latest update fixes footstep particles, and adds glazed terracotta blocks. On the technical side, it also moves from nbt to purely data components.

# ❗This Mod Is In Beta ❗
**More Dyes** is a mod aiming to infinitely* increase the range of colored blocks available to the player! By using a dye basin you can mix dyes to create any color you'd like and apply the color to various colored block types.

*Infinitely as in 16777216 color options.

![Example](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/e4c8f7aa03c4a23d80abc6e91229787867259ba7_0.webp)

# 💾 Installation
To install this mod, simply place the mod's jar file in the mods folder of your fabric installation, along side the Fabric API.

# ❓ How To Use
In order to mix a dye you will need a few things, namely a dye basin, and a dye vial. You must heat the dye basin by placing it above a fire, lava, or a magma block. After the basin is heated, and a bucket of water is placed in it, you can mix any number of vanilla dyes or custom dyes together to create new colors.

![Dye Basin Recipe](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/196c310762f838abd33d29c612def78ac9f8da32.png)
![Dye Vial Recipe](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/99311e0070087e51a226771a25d4c171b6f74970.png)

#

To extract the dye from the basin, simply right click it with an empty dye vial. The newly mixed dye can be used to mix other dyes, or to dye objects by crafting them together.

![Dyeing Example](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/fc6f6972e599fb4b53bad24e832ebdde5e1f5e67.png)

The dyed blocks can also be "rinsed" by right clicking a dye basin holding water.

**TIP: Pressing F3 + H allows you to view the color code for a dye vial or dyed item.**

# ⛔ Current Limitations

This mod is still under development. Not all features are complete. Current planned features include:

~~\> Fixing footstep particles.~~

\> Candles, and candled cakes.

\> Add vanilla equivalent recipes (e.g. glazed terracotta smelting)

~~\> Glazed terracotta.~~

\> Beds.

\> Rainbow dye.

\> Shulker boxes.

\> ⚠️ Banners. (Potentially, a lot of work, low priority.)

description: Make Richard Stallman proud by preventing minecraft from starting with non-osi approved licenses!
body:
Game-agnostic fabric mod to prevent games from starting if mods with [non-osi approved](https://opensource.org/licenses) licenses are found. If non-open-source mods are found, the game will crash, and non-compliant mods will be output to logs. 

This mod does not depend on minecraft, so it is compatible with **any game** that can be loaded with fabric loader. Thus, this mod is completely version agnostic, so it should work on any version of minecraft that fabric supports.

This mod is designed for people who care about open source, and want a way to prevent accidental downloads of (1) improperly licensed or (2) poorly licensed mods.

## False positives

In order to respect the user, this mod never attempts to make any network requests to update the license list. Thus, the license list may become outdated. **_Please report this_** to the issue tracker, and check back later for an updated version.

Additionally, many mods do not provide their license names as valid SPDX license identifiers. This may cause problems for licenses that are open source but improperly named. I attempt to handle such cases, but it's not perfect. You can fix this by simply adding the license to the configuration, but **_please report alternative spellings of license names to the issue tracker on github_**. This improves the mod for future users.

## Config

Additional licenses can be added with the configuration file, located in `config/absolutely_proprietary.json`. Mod exclusions can also be added, to whitelist specific mods.

**Configuration Keys**

**allowed_license**: List of allowed licenses. Use `@<id>` to include licenses from builtin license sets. Supported include sets: `@osi`, `@alt`, `@cc` (creative commons).

**allowed_mods**: Whitelisted mods. If whitelisted, skips license checks. Use `@<id>` to include mods from builtin mod sets. Supported include sets: (none).

**fallback_to_parent**: If `true`, will attempt to fallback licenses for mods without licenses that are embedded in another mod.

**whitelist_builtin**: If `true`, builtin things like `java` will be whitelisted. This should be true for most cases.

title: Better `rsqrt`
description: Replaces the constants Minecraft uses for their functions for calculating the reciprocal square root (aka rsqrt) with more accurate alternatives
body:
# Better `rsqrt`
**N.B.:** The accuracy benefits of this is negligible at best, so don't expect anything big to happen. This is created
purely because I want to, and I can. 

*Tested to work every version since 1.14 (v1.0.1)*

Replaces the constant Minecraft uses in their [fast reciprocal square root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_inverse_square_root)
(also known as `InvSqrt` or `rsqrt`) functions, to yield better accuracy:

| Function | Original Value | More Accurate™ Value |
|----------|----------------|---------------------|
|`fastInverseSqrt(float)`| `0x5f3759df` | `0x5f375a86`|
|`fastInverseSqrt(double)`| `0x5fe6eb50c7b537aa` | `0x5fe6eb50c7b537a9`|

Since Minecraft only use these functions in rendering, this "fix" should not affect world generation or other functions
that rely on the vanilla result to yield expected results.

### References
Both accessed on June 13th, 2021:
- [Lomont, C. (2003). Fast Inverse Square Root](https://lomont.org/papers/2003/InvSqrt.pdf)
- [Robertson, M. (2012). A Brief History of InvSqrt](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~m32rober/rsqrt.pdf)

title: mob_controller
description: Let all mobs fight for you.
body:
Missing you, pet plugin.
This mod adds multiple items for taming all mobs.

Main Features
Allows players to use "Mixed Grains" or "Inexhaustible Golden Stew" to tame mobs with health not greater than 10 points, making them fight for the player. (Configurable allowed health in config.)
Mixed Grains is consumed when used, while Inexhaustible Golden Stew is not. Their default crafting recipes have different costs. Configurable which item's recipe is enabled.
Taming materials can be customized in config, e.g., using a diamond sword to tame zombies. (Configurable required current health, taming chance, and whether the item is consumed.)
The higher the mob's health, the lower the taming chance, with a minimum of 20%.
Mobs tamed with this item can switch between Follow, Stay, and Wander states.

Follow state: When the owner is more than 8 blocks away, the mob moves toward the owner. When the owner is more than 14 blocks away, the mob teleports to the owner (terrestrial mobs teleport only to air blocks, aquatic mobs only to water; configurable teleport types, including amphibious).

Stay state: Stays in place, does not move.

Wander state: Uses the mob's original pathfinding AI to wander aimlessly.

Other Features
Mobs with health greater than 150 points can only be tamed one per player per type (configurable health threshold).
Mobs that are already tamable by vanilla or other mods cannot be tamed by this item (including some mod pets that have pet tags but no taming method).
Mobs tamed by this item gain very fast regeneration when out of combat or not taking void damage, healing 1 health point every 2 ticks (configurable out-of-combat delay). Out of combat means losing仇恨 and not being hit for 0.5 seconds.
Most mobs tamed by this item lose their ability to break blocks.
Ravagers, hoglins, zoglins, guardians, elder guardians, dolphins, goats, sniffers, polar bears, pandas, cows, and sheep are rideable after taming.
Tamed wandering traders no longer disappear, and their trade lists restock infinitely (configurable).
Tamed witches throw healing and instant health potions based on the health of the player and the player's pets.
Tamed piglins, piglin brutes, and hoglins no longer zombify. Tamed piglins no longer pick up "gold items" but only "gold ingots".
Tamed witches and piglins throw fire resistance potions at other tamed mobs and the owner that are on fire.
Vexes summoned by tamed evokers are also tamed, but these vexes do not respawn or regenerate via mod features.
Helmets on tamed zombies and skeletons no longer lose durability in daylight.
All mobs tamed by this item become neutral to other mobs (e.g., tamed illagers do not attack iron golems).
All mobs become neutral to mobs tamed by this item (e.g., iron golems do not attack tamed illagers).
Mobs tamed by this item do not attack other tamed mobs of the same owner or pets of the same owner.
All mobs tamed by this item cannot pick up equipment.
Tamed illagers do not join raids.
Added Jade integration to display current mode and owner.
Mobs tamed by this item respawn after death and teleport to the owner's location (configurable respawn cooldown, default 30 seconds).
Small slimes and small magma cubes split from tamed slimes and magma cubes are also tamed, but these small ones do not respawn.
Configurable special mobs that are forced to stay in place when in Stay state (generally for aquatic or flying mobs that may have pathfinding issues; use with caution due to forceful method).
Mobs tamed by this mod do not disappear in Peaceful mode.
Honeycomb can be used on water-sensitive mobs (e.g., endermen). Waxed mobs take no damage from contact with water.

Armor Blueprint
Allows editing the armor, main hand, and offhand items of mobs tamed by this mod.

Beast Tamer's Whistle
Controls the state of all mobs tamed by this mod within a 32-block radius. Left-click switches to Follow, middle-click switches to Wander, right-click switches to Stay. Affected mobs glow for five seconds.

Dark Stew
Untames a mob (only the owner can untame their mob).

Cavalry Flute
Left-click to select mob A, then left-click mob B to make mob A ride mob B.
Mob A must be a mob tamed by this mod or the player's pet (owner must be the player).
Mob B must be a mob tamed by this mod, the player's pet (owner must be the player), or a horse (no need to tame).

War Horn
Switches between Aggressive Mode and Protective Mode.
Left-click or right-click to switch a single mob's mode.
Sneak + left-click or right-click to switch the mode of all mobs within 32 blocks.

Protective Mode: Like wolves, attacks mobs that attack the owner or that the owner attacks, and反击 when attacked by other mobs.

Aggressive Mode: On top of Protective Mode behavior, actively attacks all nearby hostile mobs.

Legion Banner
Left-click or right-click on air to cycle the player's team color.
Left-click or right-click on a mob tamed by this mod to make them enter Legion Mode.
Middle-click to make the player themselves enter Legion Mode.

Legion Mode: All mobs tamed by the same player can only be in the same team. Players and mobs in Legion Mode get an outline and Jade display matching their team color. Tamed mobs of different teams attack each other (Aggressive Mode is disabled in Legion Mode).

Come on, who doesn't want a Legion battle royale.

title: Graphite
description: A Vulkan-based rendering engine for Minecraft 1.8.9
body:
Graphite

A Vulkan-based renderer for Minecraft: Java Edition 1.8.9

--- ## Overview Graphite is a Fabric mod that replaces Minecraft’s default OpenGL renderer with a fully rewritten Vulkan 1.3 renderer. This is not a wrapper or translation layer. It is a complete rewrite of the rendering system, built to better match modern GPU architectures and reduce CPU overhead. --- ## Why Graphite? - Replaces the legacy OpenGL 2.1 renderer with Vulkan 1.3 - Lower CPU overhead and better frame pacing - Designed for modern GPUs and drivers - Opens the door for more advanced rendering techniques --- ## Installation ### Requirements - Ornithe modloader ### Steps 1. Install Ornithe 2. Download the latest Graphite release from this repository 3. Place the jar file into your `.minecraft/mods` folder 4. Launch the game --- ## Links - Download: https://modrinth.com/mod/graphite - Discord: https://discord.gg/gMHVnMBEMh --- ## Notes - This project is experimental and still in development - Expect bugs, crashes, and incomplete features - Please report issues with logs attached --- ## Licensing This project includes code derived from Sodium. Both Graphite and Sodium are licensed under Polyform Shield 1.0.0. - Graphite license applies to original code in Graphite - Sodium license applies to any reused or adapted portions from Sodium - Graphite's modifications and additions are licensed under the same terms as Sodium, but those protections apply to us as well An exception to this is the `vulkan-api` module, which is licensed under a custom license.

title: Mystcraft Reborn
description: Explore user-written dimensions, craft fast-travel portals, take in-game photos and videos.
body:
<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/6k7D_ISsC0Q" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

Mystcraft Reborn is a modern re-interpretation of the classic Mystcraft mod. With mechanics inspired by Myst (1993), players can write new dimensions, linked together with teleportation books and portals. Players can also take photos and videos with the camera item, which are printed into picture books. The camera doubles as an easy telescope for zooming in and out. Mystcraft Reborn is designed to be a well-balanced addition to survival-friendly modpacks.

**Get started with making new worlds (Ages):**
- Craft a notebook
- Collect biomes into the notebook by finding one, then capture it by opening the book there. A notebook can store up to 16 biomes. 
- Craft a new descriptive book
- At the writing desk, place a notebook into the left slot, then an empty descriptive book into the right slot. Clicking the symbols from the notebook's biome inventory will queue them for transfer to the empty descriptive book. Alternatively, in creative mode, you can spawn a notebook with all biomes available. To make a fully upgraded writing desk, use a biome encyclopedia to store all of your collected biomes in one place.
- Finalize your selection at the writing desk. You can also remove individual biomes from the transfer queue on the right.
- Remove the descriptive book from the writing desk to finalize it. You can leave the notebook in the desk to make a dedicated authoring station. 
- Open the descriptive book to initialize the new Mystcraft age, which will only use the biomes listed on its originating descriptive book. **Once you open a descriptive book, it cannot be edited at the editing table.**
- Click the page to travel to the new age. You can exit using a rewinding book, linking book, or a descriptive book for a different age.

**How to fast travel:**
- Place a book into the crafting table to make a linking book. Once the linking book is removed from the crafting table, it will record a 2-second video clip of your environment. This will be used as the linking book's preview, which can be placed into item frames for animated displays. 
- Open the linking book and click the page to fast travel to where the linking book was crafted.
- Optional: use rewinding book or portals for two-way transit. 

**How to make a portal:**
- Create a nether-portal-style frame from any crystal block color, with a book receptacle occupying one of the portal-facing blocks. Make sure the receptacle is facing outwards, or upwards if placed at the bottom row of the portal frame. You can also make 3-dimensional portal frames for cube-shaped linking portals.
- Place a descriptive book or linking book into the receptacle. Linking portal blocks will fill the frame.
- Optional: Adjust frame and portal color with a coloring book.

**How to use the camera:**
- Select the camera in your hotbar. 
- Press the scroll wheel once to enter telephoto mode. The player can zoom in and out using the scroll wheel. To exit this mode, click the scroll wheel again.
- To take a photo or video, right-click with the camera equipped. You must have at least one piece of paper in your inventory to print the capture onto. When the camera is used, it will ask if you want to take a photo or video. Photos are stored in higer resolution than videos due to Mineraft's item size limit. If video is selected, you'll be prompted to enter a video clip length. Keep in mind this will affect file size. When capturing photo or video, a countdown is displayed before capture. 
- Once your capture has been finalized, a piece of paper is consumed from the player's inventory and transformed into a picture book.
- Picture books that have a photo inside of them can be opened. To view the full-screen image or animation, click the page while its open.

**How to manage your Mystcraft Reborn data:**
- To delete a linking book or picture book, insert them into the book shredding receptacle. 
- To delete an entire mystcraft age, insert its descriptive book into the shredding receptacle. You'll be prompted for confirmation, then the age will be permanently deleted. This will deactivate all portals and books that link to the deleted age. 

**How to display books / create signs / holograms:**
- Place a picture book or linking book into a book player block to display photos or videos via hologram. Alternatively, books can be put into item frames for display, but will have significantly less features.
- After inserting a book, you can right-click the book player block to adjust how your book's media is displayed. Holograms can be up to 36x36 blocks in size, and offset by 17.5 blocks in any direction. In addition to facing any direction, book players can also be used on floors and ceilings - intended for use as custom rugs or skylights.

**How to use the printing table:**
- The printing table is an alternative style of crafting table designed for Mystcraft book operations. The printing table has a similar interface to the Anvil, but differs in key ways. This table is very powerful, allowing the user to easily clone books of any type, transfer media across books, load images from the internet for ingame signage, and consolidate notebooks into biome encyclopedias. If the wrong recipe is used, as of Beta 1.4 the printing table will spit out items instead of overriding them, then recommends alternative crafting recipes if any are possible with the items remaining.
- To clone books, place a book into the left slot. Then place an emerald into the center slot. A cloned book will appear in the right slot. Both books can be left within the table for storage, or withdrawn.
- To transfer media across books, place the book with media you wish to transfer on the left. Then, place the book with media you wish to replace on the right. Then, place a piece of paper in the center slot. Think of it like transfer paper. Both books can be left within the table for storage, or withdrawn. 
- To transfer online images to Mystcraft books, paste an image URL into an empty vanilla book or book & quill item. Then, put the book into the left slot of the printing table. Then, place a piece of paper into the middle slot. The submitted book will transform into a picture book with the image attached. This can be used to display any image with item frames or the book player block. The picture book can be left within the table for storage, or withdrawn.
- To consolidate notebooks into biome encyclopedias, place a notebook with biomes into the printing table's left slot, then the biome encyclopedia into the right slot. Then place one piece of paper into the center slot. This will delete the notebook and append its biomes into the encyclopedia. The biome encyclopedia can be left within the table for storage, or withdrawn.


**How to use the editing table:**
- The editing table is an optional intermediary step between using the writing desk and activating the descriptive book. 
- To create a new age with custom worldgen parameters, assign biomes to a new descriptive book with the writing desk. Then, before opening the descriptive book for the first time, place it into the editing table beaneath the checkmark confirm button.
- To adjust parameters, place a specific number of catalyst items into any of the slots. For example, to create an age with maximum turbulence, insert 16 diamonds. To create an age with minimum turbulence, insert just 1 diamond. All parameters have 16 levels, represented by the number of each catalyst item inserted. Any parameter not directly edited will remain randomized, as shown by the editing table interface.
- You can leave the editing table at any time to gather more catalyst items. Because of the number of items required, its recommend to have a dedicated area for Mystcraft tables with chests holding the resources they consume. 
- Once the confirm button is pressed, the descriptive book is placed into the player's inventory. Open the descriptive book, then click the page after a few seconds to enter the new age.

**Pro Tips**
- Create multiple "sister ages" by cloning descriptive books before their first use.
- Create rugs by downloading an online texture via printing table, then placing a book player into the floor. Use the rotation feature to give the illusion of a crooked rug.
- Mystcraft allows players to obtain mob spawners in survival by mining them with silk touch. Place a spawner item into the editing table to make an age without any mobs.
- When a linking book is used, all entities within a 6 block radius travel alongside the player. This can be used for easy entity capture.
- Carry a book bag instead of sacrificing inventory space to Mystcraft books.
- Use a head lamp to explore dark ages.

**Things to keep in mind:**
- This mod was built on top of Mystcraft Ageless, an alpha prototype made for a competition in 2024. Mystcraft Reborn is my attempt to fix the unfinished / broken code in Ageless, and heavily expand it according to my own vision for what Mystcraft could be. 
- I went through great lengths to optimize server data transmission due to picture books being up to 500kb in size. All books are cached on the client-side GPU and not reloaded. In testing I haven't seen any issues with bandwidth usage or packet failures. However, **you might need mod like Packet Fixer if you intend to fill a large chest with full-length (20sec) videos.** Otherwise the per-chunk NBT data could go beyond the vanilla 8MB netty handler limit, causing players to disconnect upon opening the chest. I couldn't reproduce this bug in my testing, but it's theoretically possible. Linking books are compressed down to 30kb, so this issue only applies to having large amounts of picture books with max-length video clips.
- Mystcraft Reborn was extensively tested with NeoForge 1.21.1 servers, and is fully compatible with servers in Mystcraft Reborn Beta 1.0.1 or newer. 
- It is highly recommended to use JEI mod to view crafting recipies.

**Required Mods:**
1. Kotlin for Forge

**Nearly 300 mods have been used alongside Mystcraft Reborn without issue, but these are explicitly compatible:**
- Terralith
- Terrablender
- Wover
- Biomes O Plenty
- Better Nether
- Better End
- Minecolonies
- Better Archeology

title: Speedrunning A Random Item
description: Challenge yourself to obtain a randomly selected item as fast as possible — with twists. Roll complications like No Sprinting, Meat Only, Inverted Mouse, or No Armor and race agains
body:
#  Speedrunning A Random Item

A singleplayer challenge mod for Minecraft 1.21.11.  
Roll a random target item, pick a complication, and get it as fast as you can.
This mod almost completely repeats the rubric of the YouTuber KompotikIvun

## How it works

When you create a world, a new **Random** tab appears in the world creation screen.  
Roll a random item and a random complication, then start the world.  
The timer starts on your first input — mouse movement or keypress.  
Collect the required number of the target item to stop the clock.

## Complications

27 complications that make the run harder (or just weirder):

| Category | Complications |
|---|---|
| **Movement** | Snail (no sprinting), Giant (×2 size), Midget (×0.5 size) |
| **Vision** | Mole (min render distance), Noir (black & white shader), Cockeyed (inverted mouse) |
| **Diet** | Vegetarian (no meat), Carnivore (meat only) |
| **Inventory** | Holes in Pockets (hotbar only), One-armed (no offhand), Fragile Bones (no armor) |
| **World** | Vastness (Large Biomes), Maximalism (Amplified) |
| **Danger** | Hydrophobe (instant death in water), Thalassophobe (pushed away from oceans) |
| **Sensitivity** | Turtle (min mouse sensitivity), Sonic (max mouse sensitivity) |
| **Social** | Antisocial (villagers won't trade), Insomnia (can't sleep) |
| **Perspective** | Protagonist (first person only), NPC (third person only) |
| **Misc** | Deafness (no sound), Acceleration (×2 tickrate), Ignoramus (no recipe book), Twins (collect ×2), Triplets (collect ×3) |

## Features

- **In-game HUD** — shows target item, active complication, and live timer
- **Death screen shortcuts** — restart with the same seed or roll a new one instantly
- **Manual selection** — don't want a random pick? Browse and choose any item or complication manually
- **Persistent timer** — leaving and rejoining the world doesn't reset your time
- **Attempt tracking** — worlds are automatically named with attempt numbers on restart

title: TempBuild
description: Extension to WorldGuard to create temporary building zones. Blocks placed in designated regions automatically decay after a configurable time period.
body:
Extension to **WorldGuard** to create temporary building zones. Blocks placed in designated regions automatically decay after a configurable time period. ## Supported Platforms
## Features - **WorldGuard Integration**: Adds custom `temp-build` region flag - **Automatic Block Decay**: Blocks placed in temp-build zones disappear after configured time - **Visual Feedback**: Shows block damage progress as decay timer counts down - **Configurable Drop Behavior**: Choose whether decaying blocks drop items or vanish ## Dependencies - [WorldGuard](https://dev.bukkit.org/projects/worldguard) - Region protection and custom flags ## WorldGuard Flag Usage TempBuild adds a custom WorldGuard flag called `temp-build`. ### Setting Up a Temporary Build Region ```bash # Allow temporary building in a region /region flag temp-build allow # Disable temporary building (default behavior) /region flag temp-build deny ``` ### ⚠️ IMPORTANT For the `temp-build` flag to work properly, you must ensure that no other WorldGuard flags are blocking block placement in the region. If players still cannot place blocks despite `temp-build` being set to ALLOW, check for conflicting flags like `passthrough`, `build`, or other protection flags that may be preventing block placement. ## Configuration Options | Option | Type | Default | Description | |--------|------|---------|-------------| | `blockDecayTime` | Integer | `30` | Duration in seconds that blocks remain before decaying. Set to `0` or negative to disable decay entirely. | | `dropBlocks` | Boolean | `true` | When `true`, blocks drop their items when the timer expires. When `false`, blocks simply vanish. | | `protectFromExplosions` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, blocks in the region are protected from explosion damage. | | `allowFireBurn` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, fire can burn and destroy blocks in the region. | | `allowFireIgnite` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, fire can be ignited in the region. | | `allowBlockSpread` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, blocks like fire and mushrooms can spread within the region. | | `allowReplaceNonCollidableBlocks` | Boolean | `true` | When `true`, players can replace non-solid blocks (like grass, flowers, etc.) in the region. | | `allowLiquidFlow` | Boolean | `false` | When `true`, water and lava can flow within the region. | | `allowReplaceLiquids` | Boolean | `true` | When `true`, players can place blocks in liquid spaces. **Warning**: This also prevents placing blocks on water surfaces. | | `blockedBlocks` | List | `[]` | List of block types (e.g., `TNT`, `OBSIDIAN`) that cannot be placed in temporary build regions. | ## Commands | Command | Description | Permission | |---------|-------------|------------| | `/tempbuild reload` | Reload plugin configuration | `tempbuild.command.reload` | ## Permissions | Permission | Description | Default | |------------|-------------|---------| | `tempbuild.command.reload` | Allows reloading the plugin configuration | `op` |

title: maxHearts
description: MaxHearts is a fully customizable health plugin that adds permanent hearts, player progression, lifesteal, death-loss, revive tokens, heart items, trap (TNT, lava, dripstone), combat tagging, economy heart purchases, and offline support & more...
body:
# MaxHearts

MaxHearts is a fully-featured heart management system for Paper/Spigot servers.  
It permanently adjusts a player’s true maximum health attribute (not just temporary effects), so hearts display correctly on the HUD, persist across sessions, and work with any survival or RPG server.

Every feature in MaxHearts is fully configurable.  
You can run it as a lightweight “set/give/take hearts” plugin, or enable its advanced systems like lifesteal, traps, revive tokens, combat tagging, Vault purchasing, and more.

All features work together seamlessly — or you can toggle off anything you don’t want. You'll want to visit the config.yml file on this one.

![Showcase of the ability to raise a users maximum health above the vanilla 10 hearts which is perfect for hardcore servers ](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/86cb51dadd882dc86e3d26514edb9d42e1b371f0.png)

---

## Features

### Core Heart System
- Set, give, take, donate, transfer, or withdraw hearts
- Supports offline players, UUID-based storage, and custom floors/limits
- Persistent values survive restarts, deaths, and relogs

### Lifesteal (Multiple Layers)
- Basic PvP lifesteal  
- Projectile lifesteal (toggleable)  
- Tamed-mob lifesteal (toggleable)  
- **Trap Lifesteal:** TNT, lava traps, and falling pointed dripstone properly credit the true killer  
- Full cooldown, per-day cap, opt-out bypass, and permission controls

### Death Penalties
- Configurable heart loss on death  
- Floor actions: block / kick / ban / clamp  
- Supports “Last Stand” style plugins without conflict  
- Offline-safe — pending heart changes apply cleanly on next login

### Revive System
- Craftable **Revive Token** (fully configurable recipe, name, lore, model data)  
- Required or optional for reviving banned players  
- Prevents item duping/spoofing via PDC tagging  
- Restores players from MaxHearts bans with configurable heart amount

### Economy Integration (Vault)
- Players can buy hearts using money  
- Supports flat or progressive pricing  
- Daily caps & cooldowns  
- Works through commands, menus, shops, or NPCs

### Heart Items
- Configurable **Heart Shard** crafting  
- Configurable **Heart Item** consumable for gaining hearts  
- Optional Survival-only use  
- Custom display name, lore, and model data

### Combat Tagging
- Lightweight combat tagging system  
- Chat notifications for entering & leaving combat  
- Optional PvP logout protection  
- Fully configurable timing & messages

### Offline & Scale-Safe
- No database required  
- Efficient UUID/YAML storage  
- Safe for large servers  
- Auto-cleans old daily counters  
- Compatible with last stand plugins

---

## Why MaxHearts?

- Extremely customizable — every feature can be toggled independently  
- Zero dependencies required (Vault & PAPI optional)  
- Offline-player support by default  
- Perfect for survival, hardcore, lifesteal SMPs, factions, RPG, and quest servers  
- Lightweight and easy to integrate with other plugins, datapacks, or scripts  

---

## Commands & Permissions

| Command | Permission | Description |
|--------|------------|-------------|
| `/maxhearts set <player> <hearts>` | maxhearts.set | Set a player’s hearts |
| `/maxhearts give <player> <amount>` | maxhearts.give | Give hearts |
| `/maxhearts take <player> <amount>` | maxhearts.take | Remove hearts |
| `/maxhearts donate <player> <amount>` | maxhearts.donate | Donate hearts |
| `/maxhearts transfer <from> <to> <amount>` | maxhearts.transfer | Transfer hearts between players |
| `/maxhearts withdraw <amount>` | maxhearts.withdraw | Turn hearts into a shard item |
| `/maxhearts revive <player> [hearts]` | maxhearts.revive | Revive & unban a player (requires token if enabled) |
| `/maxhearts buy <amount>` | maxhearts.buy | Buy hearts with Vault |
| `/maxhearts lifesteal on/off` | maxhearts.lifesteal | Toggle lifesteal participation |
| `/maxhearts combat` | maxhearts.combat | Check remaining combat tag time |

title: MCMMORewards
description: A lightweight plugin that allows server administrators to configure rewards (console commands) that are executed when a player reaches a specific level in an mcMMO skill.
body:
# McMMORewards

McMMORewards is a lightweight Minecraft plugin that allows server administrators to configure rewards (console commands) that are executed when a player reaches a specific level in an mcMMO skill.

## Features

- **Skill-Based Rewards**: Define rewards for any mcMMO skill (Mining, Herbalism, Acrobatics, etc.).
- **Level-Specific**: Trigger rewards at exact levels (e.g., Level 10, 50, 100).
- **Multiple Commands**: Execute multiple console commands for a single reward.
- **Placeholders**: Use `%player%` to target the player who leveled up.
- **Reload Command**: Reload configuration without restarting the server.

## Requirements

- **Java 17+**
- **Spigot/Paper 1.20+**
- **mcMMO**: This plugin requires mcMMO to be installed and running.

## Installation

1. Download the `McMMORewards.jar`.
2. Place it in your server's `plugins` folder.
3. Ensure you have `mcMMO` installed.
4. Restart your server.

## Configuration

The `config.yml` allows you to define rewards.

```yaml
rewards:
  mining:
    10:
      - "give %player% diamond 1"
      - "broadcast %player% has reached Mining level 10!"
    50:
      - "eco give %player% 500"
      - "broadcast %player% reached Mining 50!"
  herbalism:
    25:
      - "give %player% golden_apple 1"
```

- **Root key**: `rewards`
- **Skill Name**: (e.g., `mining`, `herbalism`). Must match mcMMO skill names (case-insensitive).
- **Level**: The integer level at which the reward triggers.
- **Commands**: A list of console commands to run. Do not include `/`.

## Commands

- `/mcmmorewards reload` - Reloads the `config.yml` file.

## Permissions

- `mcmmorewards.reload` - Allows access to the reload command (Default: OP).

title: RedFox's UHC
description: Setup Minecraft UHC in Your world Easily !
body:
**UHC Pack for Minecraft Java Edition**


A datapack for Minecraft Java Edition for running Ultra Hardcore (UHC) tournaments.
# 
**Currently supported Minecraft versions:**

1.21.x
1.20.x
1.19.x
1.18.x

Earlier versions are not compatible due to the use of new command in the datapack. More recent versions (including snapshots) may be compatible but are not actively supported until a stable release is available.
# 
**How to setup :**

Download the zip file for the latest release of the datapack.

Place the zip file in in the <world>/datapacks/ folder.

Run **/reload** (or **/minecraft:reload** on Spigot/Paper) on your server to detect the new datapack

Decide the center of your map and teleport to it e.g. **/tp @s 0 ~ 0**

Run **/function uhc_pack:setup** to prepare the Lobby

From here, you can control the rest of the setup from the book provided.
# 

By default, only the player who set up will be able to start the UHC or change settings. If you need to grant other players the ability to do this, you can by running /tag <PlayerName> add admin.

Once a player has died they will be placed into spectator mode. If you wish to allow them to be respawned (for example, due to a death caused by server lag), you can by running execute as <PlayerName> run function uhc_pack:respawn.

After the UHC has concluded, you can run /function uhc_pack:complete to put everyone into spectator mode and lock in the awards. You can then reveal the awards using /function uhc_pack:awards/reveal.
#
**Features :**

**Team selection** - Allow players to select their own teams as well as allow for them to be randomized between a specified number of teams. Players can also choose to spectate only. Players who join after the game has started automatically spectate.

**World configuration** - Pick from a number of world sizes, from 500-3K blocks wide. Chunks can also be pre-generated to avoid lag during gameplay. To encourage combat, you can also configure a shrinking border with control over when it starts shrinking, the duration it shrinks for and the eventual border size.

**Minute markers** - To help keep track of time, minute markers can be configured.

**Late game options** - Encourage teams to engage in PVP by triggering external day and glowing effects.

**Buffs and Nerfs** - Control the balance of your UHC using toggles for whether strong potions or suspicious stews are allowed.

**Extensible** - Event triggers are available to allow other datapacks to plugin to UHC to further customize the experience.

#

title: Infinite Villager Trades
description: Unlock infinite trading with villagers! This plugin removes trade limits, allowing players unlimited access to merchant recipes. Perfect for survival servers, creative mode, and admin tools.
body:
# Infinite Villager Trades Plugin - Full Description

## What is This Plugin?

**Infinite Villager Trades** is a Minecraft server plugin designed for Paper/Spigot servers running Minecraft 1.21.11 and above. It completely removes trading limitations with villagers, allowing players to trade infinitely without the standard merchant trade restrictions.

By default, Minecraft villagers have a limited number of trades they can perform before requiring a restock period. This plugin eliminates that restriction entirely, making villagers an unlimited resource for trading.

## Core Features

### 🔄 Unlimited Trading
- Instantly removes all trade limits from any villager
- No cooldown or restock timer
- Works on all villager types (librarians, cartographers, masons, etc.)
- Trades reset to available every time a villager is interacted with

### ⚡ Instant Activation
- No commands or configuration needed
- Works automatically when players open a villager's trading interface
- Real-time event-based system
- Zero performance overhead

### 🎯 Universal Compatibility
- Works with all villager professions
- Compatible with all merchant types
- No conflicting dependencies
- Lightweight and efficient

## How It Works

When a player opens a villager's trading menu:
1. The plugin detects the inventory opening event
2. It identifies the merchant (villager) holding that inventory
3. For each trading recipe offered:
   - Sets the recipe's maximum uses to `Integer.MAX_VALUE` (unlimited)
   - Resets the current uses to `0` (full availability)
4. The modified recipes are applied back to the merchant instantly

This happens seamlessly in the background without any visual changes or notifications.

## Use Cases

### 🏞️ Survival Servers
Enable endless access to valuable trades like enchanted books, rare items, and resources without waiting for villagers to restock. Perfect for progression servers where specific items are crucial.

### 🎨 Creative Servers
Remove all barriers to accessing merchant goods, allowing creative builders and admins unlimited resource acquisition for construction and testing.

### 🛠️ Admin Tools
Simplify admin workflows by providing unlimited access to hard-to-find items through merchants without needing WorldEdit or other world-modification tools.

### 🎮 Custom Gamemodes
Build custom gamemodes where villager trading is central to progression, without the artificial limitations of vanilla trading mechanics.

### 📊 Economy Servers
Perfect complement to economy plugins where villager trading serves as a baseline for item valuation.

## Technical Specifications

### Requirements
- **Java:** Version 21+
- **Server Software:** Paper or Spigot
- **Minecraft Version:** 1.21.11+ (1.21.x compatible)
- **Dependencies:** None (built-in Bukkit API)

### Performance
- Minimal CPU usage (event-based, not looping)
- No database or file I/O operations
- Negligible RAM footprint
- Single-threaded, safe implementation

### Installation
1. Download or build the plugin JAR file
2. Place it in your server's `plugins/` directory
3. Restart the server
4. Plugin loads automatically with no configuration required

### Building from Source
```
mvn clean package
```
The compiled JAR will be in the `target/` directory.

## File Structure

```
├── InfiniteVillagerTrades121X.java
│   ├── onEnable()           - Plugin initialization
│   ├── onDisable()          - Plugin shutdown
│   └── onInventoryOpen()    - Event handler for infinite trades
└── plugin.yml               - Plugin metadata
```

## Event System

The plugin uses Bukkit's event system with a single event handler:

**Event:** `InventoryOpenEvent`
- **Trigger:** When any inventory is opened
- **Action:** Checks if inventory holder is a Merchant
- **Modification:** Applies infinite uses to all recipes
- **Performance:** Minimal check, instant processing

## Compatibility Notes

✅ **Compatible With:**
- All Bukkit-based servers (Paper, Spigot, Purpur, etc.)
- All plugin versions that use standard Bukkit API
- All trader types (villagers, wandering traders, custom merchants)
- All item types and enchantment combinations

❌ **Not Compatible With:**
- Vanilla/pure Bukkit versions (use Paper or Spigot fork)
- Minecraft versions below 1.21.11

## Customization & Extension

The plugin code is straightforward and can be modified for:
- Specific trade limitations (trade limit per recipe instead of infinite)
- Selective villager filtering (only certain professions)
- Custom pricing or trade modifications
- Integration with economy plugins
- Custom logging or tracking systems

## Troubleshooting

**Issue:** Plugin doesn't load
- **Solution:** Ensure you're using Paper/Spigot 1.21.11+
- **Solution:** Check console for Java version errors

**Issue:** Trades are still limited
- **Solution:** Make sure you have the latest JAR file built
- **Solution:** Verify plugin is listed when running `/plugins` command

**Issue:** Server crashes
- **Solution:** This is extremely unlikely; the plugin has minimal code
- **Solution:** Check that no other trading plugins are conflicting

## Future Development

Potential enhancements:
- Configuration file for customizable trade limits
- Per-profession settings
- Trade logging and statistics
- Integration with permission systems
- GUI configuration system
- Custom trade recipe support

## Support & Contributions

For issues, feature requests, or contributions:
- Review the plugin code in the repository
- Test thoroughly before deploying to production servers
- Monitor server logs for any error messages

## License & Author

**Author:** TherogueO

Visit Plugin Hub for more plugins: 
https://discord.gg/FzD9b5nH27

---

**Version:** 1.0.0-villagertradesinf  
**Release Date:** 2026  
**Last Updated:** May 28, 2026

This plugin is designed for Minecraft server administrators and players who want a seamless, zero-config solution for unlimited villager trading.

title: YoTPA
description: YoTPA is a lightweight and powerful teleport request plugin with adaptive performance optimization. Simple to use, easy to configure, and built for modern Minecraft servers.
body:
![Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PhyschicWinter9/YoTPA/refs/heads/main/screenshot/yotpa.png)

# YoTPA

YoTPA is a lightweight and powerful teleport request plugin with adaptive performance optimization. Simple to use, easy to configure, and built for modern Minecraft servers.

## Features

### Adaptive Performance System
The plugin automatically detects your server's available RAM and optimizes itself accordingly - zero configuration needed!

**4 Performance Modes:**
- **ULTRA_LIGHT** - For 512 MB - 1 GB RAM (Free/Cheap VPS)
  - Best for: 5-10 players, minimal plugins
- **LIGHT** - For 1-2 GB RAM (Low-end servers)
  - Best for: 10-15 players, light plugins
- **BALANCED** - For 2-4 GB RAM (Mid-range servers)
  - Best for: 15-25 players, moderate plugins
- **HIGH_PERFORMANCE** - For 4+ GB RAM (High-end servers)
  - Best for: 25+ players, any plugins

**Performance Benefits:**
- 30-70% less memory usage
- 25-60% less CPU usage
- Up to 83% faster maintenance tasks
- Dynamic optimization based on your server specs

### Core Features

- **Simple TPA System** - Request to teleport to other players or invite them to you
- **Countdown Timer** - Configurable delay before teleporting with visual feedback
- **Title Display** - Clear visual indication of teleport countdown
- **Movement Detection** - Teleport cancels if player moves during countdown
- **Custom Sound Effects** - Fully customizable audio feedback using Minecraft's sound registry
- **Config Validation** - Prevents server crashes from broken configs with detailed error messages
- **Permission System** - Fine-grained access control
- **Request Management** - Toggle receiving requests, cancel outgoing requests
- **Multi-Threading Support** - Thread-safe for more concurrent players
- **Customizable Messages** - Fully localizable and configurable messages

### Internationalization (NEW in 1.4.0)

Customize all plugin messages in any language with full MiniMessage support:

```yaml
prefix: "[YoTPA] "

commands:
  tpa:
    sent: "Teleport request sent to {target}"
    received: "{requester} wants to teleport to you."
```
**MiniMessage Features:**
- Rich text formatting (bold, italic, underlined)
- Color gradients: `<gradient:green:aqua>text</gradient>`
- Rainbow effect: `<rainbow>text</rainbow>`
- Hex colors: `<#FF5733>text</#FF5733>`

### Custom Sound Effects

Customize all plugin sounds using Minecraft's sound IDs:

```yaml
sounds:
  countdown: "block.note_block.pling"
  success: "entity.enderman.teleport"
  cancel: "entity.villager.no"
  request: "entity.experience_orb.pickup"
```

Test sounds in-game: `/playsound minecraft:block.note_block.pling master @s`

## Configuration

YoTPA's `config.yml` file allows you to customize various aspects of the plugin:

- Request timeout duration
- Cooldown between requests
- Teleport delay countdown
- Performance mode settings
- Sound effects for different actions
- Feature toggles (statistics, bStats, titles, sounds)

### Configuration File

```yaml
# YoTPA Configuration v1.3.0-Adaptive
# Smart Auto-Optimization for All Server Sizes

# Request timeout in seconds (how long before a request expires)
# Recommended: 30-120 seconds
request-timeout: 60

# Request cooldown in seconds (how long before sending another request)
# Recommended: 15-60 seconds
request-cooldown: 30

# Teleport delay in seconds (countdown before actual teleport)
# Recommended: 3-10 seconds
teleport-delay: 5

# Performance mode settings
performance:
  # Options: AUTO, ULTRA_LIGHT, LIGHT, BALANCED, HIGH_PERFORMANCE
  mode: AUTO

# Sound effects (use Minecraft sound names)
sounds:
  countdown: "block.note_block.pling"
  success: "entity.enderman.teleport"
  cancel: "entity.villager.no"
  request: "entity.experience_orb.pickup"

# Feature toggles
features:
  statistics: true
  bstats: true
  titles: true
  sounds: true
```

### Messages Configuration (messages.yml)
```yaml
# Customize your prefix
prefix: "[YoTPA] "

# All messages are customizable
commands:
  tpa:
    usage: "Usage: /tpa "
    sent: "Teleport request sent to {target}"
    received: "{requester} wants to teleport to you."

teleport:
  countdown:
    title: "Teleporting..."
    subtitle: "Don't move!"
    message: "Teleporting in {seconds} seconds"
```
## Customization Examples

### Change Language to Spanish

Edit `messages.yml`:
```yaml
prefix: "[YoTPA] "

commands:
  tpa:
    usage: "Uso: /tpa "
    sent: "Solicitud enviada a {target}"
    received: "{requester} quiere teletransportarse a ti."
```

Then use `/tpareload` to apply changes!

### Add Beautiful Gradients

```yaml
prefix: "✦ YoTPA ✦ "

teleport:
  countdown:
    title: "Teleporting..."
    message: "Teleporting in {seconds} seconds"
```

### Customize Colors

```yaml
prefix: "[TPA] "

commands:
  tpa:
    sent: "Request sent to {target}"
```

### Use Hex Colors

```yaml
prefix: "[YoTPA] "

teleport:
  success: "Teleported to {target} successfully!"
```

**Placeholders:**
- `{player}` - Player name
- `{target}` - Target player name
- `{requester}` - Requester player name
- `{seconds}` - Number of seconds
- `{cooldown}` - Cooldown duration



### Configuration Sections Explained

**General Settings:**
- `request-timeout` - How long (in seconds) teleport requests remain valid (recommended: 30-120)
- `request-cooldown` - Time (in seconds) before a player can send another request (recommended: 15-60)
- `teleport-delay` - Countdown time (in seconds) before teleportation happens (minimum: 1)

**Performance Settings:**
- `performance.mode` - AUTO (recommended), ULTRA_LIGHT, LIGHT, BALANCED, or HIGH_PERFORMANCE
  - AUTO automatically detects your server's RAM and selects the best mode

**Sound Settings:**
- All sounds use Minecraft's sound registry format (lowercase with dots)
- The plugin validates sounds on config reload
- Full sound list: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sounds.json

**Feature Toggles:**
- `statistics` - Enable or disable statistics tracking
- `bstats` - Enable or disable bStats metrics
- `titles` - Enable or disable title animations during countdown
- `sounds` - Enable or disable all sound effects

### Config Validation

When reloading with `/tpareload`, the plugin validates:
- YAML syntax
- All values are in valid ranges
- Sounds exist in Minecraft's registry
- Shows detailed error messages if invalid

Example validation output:
```
Configuration validation failed!
✗ teleport-delay must be at least 1 second
✗ Sound 'countdown' (invalid.sound) not found in registry

Warnings:
• request-timeout (5) is very low, recommended: 30-120

Config not applied. Fix errors and try again.
Using previous configuration.
```

## How to Edit and Reload

1. Edit the `plugins/YoTPA/config.yml` file
2. Save your changes
3. Use `/tpareload` in-game to apply changes with validation

## Commands Overview

| Command | Description | Permission |
| :------ | :---------- | :--------- |
| `/tpa <player>` | Request to teleport to another player | `yotpa.tpa` |
| `/tpaccept` | Accept a pending teleport request | `yotpa.tpaccept` |
| `/tpadeny` | Deny a pending teleport request | `yotpa.tpadeny` |
| `/tpahere <player>` | Request a player to teleport to you | `yotpa.tpahere` |
| `/tpacancel` | Cancel your outgoing teleport request | `yotpa.tpacancel` |
| `/tpatoggle` | Toggle receiving teleport requests | `yotpa.tpatoggle` |
| `/tpareload` | Reload the plugin configuration | `yotpa.reload` |
| `/tpainfo` | View plugin information and statistics | `yotpa.info` |
| `/tpastats` | View teleport statistics | `yotpa.stats` |

**Default:** All permissions are granted to all players by default.

## Detailed Commands

### TPA Command

Send a request to teleport to another player.

```
/tpa <player>
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| :-------- | :--- | :---------- |
| `player` | `string` | **Required**. The player name you want to teleport to |

**Examples:**
```
/tpa Steve      # Request to teleport to player named Steve
/tpa Alex123    # Request to teleport to player named Alex123
```

![TPA Command](https://github.com/PhyschicWinter9/YoTPA/blob/main/screenshot/tpav2.gif?raw=true)

**Notes:**
- You cannot send a request to yourself
- There is a configurable cooldown between sending requests (default: 30 seconds)
- Request will expire after a configurable time (default: 60 seconds)
- Target player will receive a notification with clickable accept/deny buttons

---

### TPAccept Command

Accept a pending teleport request from another player.

```
/tpaccept
```

No parameters required - accepts the most recent teleport request.

**Examples:**
```
/tpaccept    # Accept the pending teleport request
```

![TPAccept Command](https://github.com/PhyschicWinter9/YoTPA/blob/main/screenshot/tpaacceptv2.gif?raw=true)

**Notes:**
- Only works if you have a pending teleport request
- After accepting, the teleportation will begin with a countdown
- The player must stay still during the countdown or it will be cancelled
- If accepting a `/tpa` request, the requester will teleport to you
- If accepting a `/tpahere` request, you will teleport to the requester

---

### TPADeny Command

Deny a pending teleport request from another player.

```
/tpadeny
```

No parameters required - denies the most recent teleport request.

**Examples:**
```
/tpadeny    # Deny the pending teleport request
```

![TPADeny Command](https://github.com/PhyschicWinter9/YoTPA/blob/main/screenshot/tpadenyv2.gif?raw=true)

**Notes:**
- Only works if you have a pending teleport request
- The requester will be notified that their request was denied
- Request is immediately removed from the system

---

### TPAHere Command

Request another player to teleport to your location.

```
/tpahere <player>
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| :-------- | :--- | :---------- |
| `player` | `string` | **Required**. The player name you want to request to teleport to you |

**Examples:**
```
/tpahere Steve      # Request Steve to teleport to you
/tpahere Alex123    # Request Alex123 to teleport to you
```

![TPAHere Command](https://github.com/PhyschicWinter9/YoTPA/blob/main/screenshot/tpaherev2.gif?raw=true)

**Notes:**
- You cannot send a request to yourself
- There is a configurable cooldown between sending requests (default: 30 seconds)
- Request will expire after a configurable time (default: 60 seconds)
- The target player must accept with `/tpaccept`

---

### TPACancel Command

Cancel your outgoing teleport request.

```
/tpacancel
```

No parameters required - cancels your most recent outgoing request.

**Examples:**
```
/tpacancel    # Cancel your pending request
```

**Notes:**
- Only works if you have an active outgoing request
- The target player will be notified that the request was cancelled
- Useful if you sent a request by mistake

---

### TPAToggle Command

Toggle whether you want to receive teleport requests.

```
/tpatoggle
```

No parameters required - toggles your request reception status.

**Examples:**
```
/tpatoggle    # Toggle receiving teleport requests on/off
```

**Notes:**
- When toggled off, other players cannot send you teleport requests
- You will receive a message showing your current status
- Your setting persists across server restarts

---

### TPAReload Command

Reload the plugin configuration with validation.

```
/tpareload
```

No parameters required - reloads and validates the configuration file.

**Examples:**
```
/tpareload    # Reload the plugin configuration
```

![TPAReload Command](https://github.com/PhyschicWinter9/YoTPA/blob/main/screenshot/tpareloadv2.gif?raw=true)

**Notes:**
- Requires the `yotpa.reload` permission (default: op only)
- Validates YAML syntax and all configuration values
- Checks that all sounds exist in Minecraft's registry
- Shows detailed errors if config is invalid
- Only applies config if all validation passes
- Useful after making changes to the config.yml file

---

### TPAInfo Command

View plugin information and real-time statistics.

```
/tpainfo
```

No parameters required - displays plugin information.

**Examples:**
```
/tpainfo    # View plugin info and stats
```

**Shows:**
- Current performance mode (auto-detected based on RAM)
- Optimization level and settings
- Active teleport requests
- Ongoing teleports
- Memory usage statistics
- Plugin version

**Notes:**
- Useful for monitoring plugin performance
- Helps diagnose issues
- Shows how the plugin has optimized itself for your server

---

### TPAStats Command

View teleport statistics and usage data.

```
/tpastats
```

No parameters required - displays teleport statistics.

**Examples:**
```
/tpastats    # View teleport statistics
```

**Shows:**
- Total teleport requests sent
- Total teleport requests received
- Success rate
- Most active players
- Other usage metrics

**Notes:**
- Requires `features.statistics: true` in config
- Statistics are tracked per player
- Data persists across server restarts

## Optimization Tips

### For FREE/LOW-SPEC servers (512 MB - 1 GB):
- Keep mode as AUTO or ULTRA_LIGHT
- Limit total plugins to 5-8
- Set view-distance to 4 in server.properties
- Use Paper instead of Spigot
- Limit players to 5-10 concurrent

### For MID-RANGE servers (2-4 GB):
- Use AUTO or BALANCED mode
- Can run 10-15 plugins
- view-distance 6-8
- 15-25 players should be fine

### For HIGH-END servers (4+ GB):
- Use AUTO or HIGH_PERFORMANCE mode
- No significant plugin limitations
- view-distance 10-12
- 25+ players supported

## Performance

YoTPA is built with performance in mind:

- **Lightweight** - Minimal impact on server TPS
- **Thread-Safe** - No lag from concurrent operations
- **Memory Efficient** - Adapts to your server's resources automatically
- **Async Operations** - Non-blocking task execution
- **Lock-Free** - No race conditions or deadlocks

## Installation

1. Download the latest JAR from the releases
2. Place the JAR in your server's `plugins` folder
3. Restart your server
4. That's it! The plugin will auto-configure based on your server's specs

---
![YoTPA bstats](https://bstats.org/signatures/bukkit/yotpa.svg)

**Note:** This is my first plugin project!.

title: Shulker Eggs
description: A throwable egg for capturing mobs in item form.
body:
Shulker Eggs are a semi-balanced way to transport mobs in survival mode!

You can throw Shulker Eggs at mobs to capture them, but every egg doesn't guarantee a capture! The more health a mob has, the greater a chance there is for the capture to fail! Deal more damage to increase your chances of successfully capturing a mob!

## Recipe
![An Egg between two Shulker Shells](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/Yn7dSYjr/images/40153487d0bb90ca124c2e8296736fb678dd3b62.png)

## Configuration
The default chance you have of capturing a full-health mob can be configured by using the following command and entering a number between 0 and 100 (representing a percentage). The default value is 25, meaning full-health mobs have a 25% chance of being captured.

```
/scoreboard players set #default_capture_chance shulker_egg 25
```

title: Mob to Egg
description: SHIFT + right click with carrot on a stick to convert a mob to a spawn egg!
body:
# Mob to Egg Converter
**<font color="Gold">Transform</font>** any mob into its spawn egg with a simple **<font color="DeepSkyBlue">SHIFT + Right-click</font>**!

For anyone who wants an **easy way** to collect and **<font color="Violet">relocate mobs</font>**!

---

## 🎯 Core Features

- **Precision Targeting** - uses advanced raycast technology to accurately detect the mob you're looking at
- **80+ Mobs Supported** - works with passive, neutral, hostile, and special mobs
- **Simple Controls** - just SHIFT + Right-click with a Carrot on a Stick
- **Audio & Visual Feedback** - hear sounds and see particles when conversion is successful
- **25 Block Range** - convert mobs from up to 25 blocks away
- **Performance Optimized** - efficient raycast system that doesn't lag your game
- **No Resource Pack** - pure datapack solution, works out of the box

---

## 🎮 How to Use

1. **Get a Carrot on a Stick** - craft or obtain one from creative inventory
2. **Find a Mob** - locate the mob you want to convert
3. **Aim at the Mob** - look directly at the mob
4. **Hold SHIFT** - press and hold your sneak key
5. **Right-Click** - use your Carrot on a Stick
6. **Collect the Egg** - the mob disappears and drops its spawn egg!

---

## 📦 Installation

Follow these steps to install the datapack:

1. Download the datapack `.zip` file
2. Navigate to your Minecraft world folder
3. Place the `.zip` file in the `datapacks` folder
4. Reload the world or use `/reload` command in-game
5. You should see a **<font color="LimeGreen">confirmation message</font>** in chat!

### World Folder Location

- **Windows:** `%appdata%\.minecraft\saves\[WorldName]\datapacks`
- **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/saves/[WorldName]/datapacks`
- **Linux:** `~/.minecraft/saves/[WorldName]/datapacks`

---

## ⚙️ Requirements

| Component | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| **Minecraft Version** | 1.21.11 (Java Edition) |
| **Pack Format** | 94 |
| **Dependencies** | None |
| **Resource Pack** | Not required |

## ✨ Supported Mobs

### **<font color="LimeGreen">Passive Mobs</font>**
> Allay, Armadillo, Axolotl, Bat, Camel, Cat, Chicken, Cod, Cow, Donkey, Fox, Frog, Glow Squid, Horse, Mooshroom, Mule, Ocelot, Parrot, Pig, Pufferfish, Rabbit, Salmon, Sheep, Skeleton Horse, Sniffer, Snow Golem, Squid, Strider, Tadpole, Tropical Fish, Turtle, Villager, Wandering Trader

### **<font color="Crimson">Hostile Mobs</font>**

---

## 🤝 Compatibility

- ✅ Works in both **Survival** and **Creative** mode
- ✅ Compatible with most other datapacks
- ✅ **<font color="DeepSkyBlue">Multiplayer friendly</font>**
- ✅ Works with modded mobs that follow vanilla spawn egg naming conventions

---

## 🔧 Technical Details

### How it Works

The datapack uses:

- **Scoreboard objectives** for right-click detection
- **Predicates** for sneak detection  
- **Raycast system** for accurate mob targeting (up to 25 blocks)
- **Execute commands** for mob type detection and conversion

### File Structure

```
mob_to_egg/
├── pack.mcmeta
└── data/
    ├── minecraft/
    │   └── tags/
    │       └── function/
    │           ├── load.json
    │           └── tick.json
    └── mob_to_egg/
        ├── predicate/
        │   └── is_sneaking.json
        └── function/
            ├── load.mcfunction
            ├── tick.mcfunction
            ├── raycast.mcfunction
            ├── raycast_step.mcfunction
            ├── convert_mob.mcfunction
            ├── convert_mob_from_raycast.mcfunction
            └── spawn_egg_by_type.mcfunction
```

### Debug Commands

```
/scoreboard objectives setdisplay sidebar click
```

This will show you if right-clicks are being registered properly.

---

## 🎬 Preview

### What Happens When You Convert a Mob

When you successfully convert a mob:

- 💨 **Particle effects** appear at the mob's location
- 🔊 **Chicken egg sound** plays
- 💚 **Green success message** appears in your action bar
- 🥚 **Spawn egg** drops at the mob's location

---

## ⚠️ Known Limitations

- **Boss mobs** (Ender Dragon, Wither) cannot be converted - they don't have spawn eggs in vanilla Minecraft
- **Armor Stands** and **Item Entities** are excluded from conversion
- Requires a **Carrot on a Stick** as the interaction item (Minecraft limitation for detecting right-clicks)

title: Take It
description: Disables automatic item pickup. Pick up items using Right-Click or a configurable hotkey. Fully compatible with pickup-tracking mods (like Loot Journal).
body:
# Take It

A simple mod that changes item pickup mechanics in Minecraft.

## Features

- 🚫 **No Auto-Pickup** - Stop picking up items accidentally just by walking past them.
- 🖱️ **Click to Pick** - Right-click an item to pick it up.
- ⌨️ **Keybind Pickup** - Press **G** (configurable) to grab all items within range.
- ⚙️ **Flexible Config** - Customize the pickup radius (X, Y, Z) and toggle the mod features.

## Configuration

The configuration file is located at `config/takeit-common.toml`:
- `enableMod` - Enable/disable the mod.
- `radiusX/Y/Z` - Pickup radius per axis (default is 2 blocks).

You can change the pickup key in the standard **Controls** settings.

## Compatibility & Technical Details

Unlike similar mods (e.g., *Click2Pick*), **TakeIt** triggers the actual vanilla player pickup event rather than simply moving the item into the inventory.

This ensures full compatibility with mods that track item pickups, achievements, or statistics, such as **Loot Journal** and similar alternatives.

# Immersive Aircraft Flan Compatibility

**NOTE: THIS MOD REQUIRES IMMERSIVE AIRCRAFT AND FLAN**

Important Compatibility fixes for Immersive Aircraft and Flan
**
This mod aims to fix compatibility issues (especially the critical ones) between Immersive Aircraft and the Flan land claiming mod.**

**Current fixes**

Prevents the player from not being able to access their aircraft after unmounting it in a flan claim.

 

**How it works**

When the pilot (player) mounts an aircraft as the controlling passenger, the aircraft saves the pilot's UUID in its data. Allowing them to mount their aircraft even if they unmount it inside flan claims.

If you are aware of other incompatibilities with Immersive Aircraft and Flan please report them on the issue tracker.

title: Polypack Host
description: Automatically build, host and require all your installed polymer mods resources!
body:
Automatically build, host and require all your installed polymer mods resources!

Requires Polymer! (Of course): https://modrinth.com/mod/polymer

## Configuration `(config/polypack_host.json)`
* `hostIp`: The IP address to host the resource pack on. Leave as `null` to use the server's IP
    * Default: `null`
* `hostPort`: The port to host the resource pack on. Make sure this port is also forwarded, so it can be accessed externally.
    * Default: `8001`
* `threadCount`: The number of threads the HTTP server is allowed to use. If the server cannot keep up with the requests, this may need to be increased.
    * Default: `3`
* `randomiseUrl`: If this is set to true, it will make the client download a new version of the resource pack each time. If you have issues with players joining and being told there was a resource pack error, set this to `true`.
    * Default: `false`

## Recommended Server Properties `(server.properties)`
* Set `require-resource-pack` to `true` so the client is mostly forced to use the resource pack.
* Set `resource-pack-prompt` to something like `"Required Mod Resources""` so the player knows why the pack is required.

> ### How does this mod pack work?

**This mod pack works very simply. From my own experience, I’ve tested many popular mod packs for optimization, and in many of them I noticed a major problem: CONFLICTS BETWEEN CERTAIN MODS AND SODIUM
Such a conflict can lead to a significant drop in FPS, since the same options—such as those in the popular Sodium base mod and the More Culling mod—overlap and perform the same optimization functions, which can cause FPS to drop. but in my mod pack, I’ve checked all the technical aspects of the mods to ensure that each one performs its specific function without causing conflicts.
And to my surprise, it turned out to be very lightweight—even I wouldn’t have expected that, given that I was adding 20–30 mods for the same function.**

1. Download the mod pack for your version of Minecraft
1. Open the Modrinth app
1. Create a new instance
1. Install the build
1. Import the build
1. Select the downloaded file
1. Done

title: Manaita
description: This is a complete remake of "Manaita".It can amplify crafting results by up to 32x.
body:
# Manaita Mod

Manaita Mod is a modern recreation of a classic-style overpowered crafting mod.

It adds a set of upgradeable Manaita boards that increase crafting multipliers far beyond normal vanilla balance, letting players push ordinary recipes into increasingly exaggerated output as they progress from wood to diamond. This mod is designed for players who enjoy nostalgic, intentionally unbalanced gameplay built around large crafting multipliers and fast material growth.

![A showcase image of all 5 Manaita board tiers placed side by side: wooden, stone, iron, gold, and diamond](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/523003cf17448408fcd7ac56b03e5bc535565254.jpeg)

<details>
<summary>日本語での説明 / Japanese Description</summary>

## このMODについて

Manaita Mod(まな板Mod)は、昔懐かしい旧作まな板MODの体験を再現したものです。

木・石・鉄・金・ダイヤの5段階のまな板を追加し、通常のクラフトレシピの結果を数倍〜数十倍に増幅します。例えば、ダイヤのまな板では1回のクラフトで32個のアイテムが産出されます。

### 特徴

- **5段階のまな板**: 木(2x) → 石(4x) → 鉄(8x) → 金(16x) → ダイヤ(32x)
- **まな板な板材**: オークの板材を破壊すると確率でまな板な板材がドロップ
- **派手な成長**: クラフト結果が爆発的に増加する、意図的にバランスを崩したゲームプレイ
- **まな板用フック**: やっぱりまな板は壁に立て掛けてないとね！やっぱまな板って断崖絶ｐ((殴

### 進行ルート

1. オークの板材を破壊してまな板な板材を入手
2. 板材から木のまな板を作成
3. 素材を集めて上位のまな板へアップグレード
4. 最終的にダイヤのまな板(32x)を作成

</details>


## What This Mod Adds

- 5 Manaita board tiers:
  - `wooden`
  - `stone`
  - `iron`
  - `gold`
  - `diamond`
- A special progression item: `plate`
- Tier-by-tier upgrade recipes from lower boards to higher boards
- Increasing crafting multipliers based on board tier
- Configurable drop replacement used to obtain `plate`

## Crafting Multipliers

Each Manaita board increases the crafting multiplier:

- `wooden`: `2x`
- `stone`: `4x`
- `iron`: `8x`
- `gold`: `16x`
- `diamond`: `32x`

The core appeal of the mod is simple: the better your board, the higher your crafting multiplier becomes. Early tiers already improve production, while higher tiers push crafting into a much more excessive and overpowered style of progression.

![An image showing a Diamond Manaita turning a diamond block into diamonds.](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/781a7f2641831b29d8116418d96cc5b76fab4ba2.png)

## Progression

Manaita Mod is built around straightforward, satisfying escalation.

You begin with the lower Manaita tiers, gather the materials needed to upgrade them, and unlock increasingly stronger crafting multipliers as you move upward through stone, iron, gold, and diamond. This creates a clear progression path where each upgrade noticeably changes how much value you get from ordinary crafting recipes.

## `plate` and Drop Behavior

`plate` is a key item in the Manaita progression system.

By default, it is obtained through configurable drop replacement. When breaking `Oak Planks`, the normal drop can be replaced with `plate` based on the following setting:

- `plateDropChance`: `0.125`

![An image showing Oak Planks being broken and `plate` appearing as the drop](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/1cfa68cef9b9b3287b8a153edefcdf51bff0b555.jpeg)

## Project Goal

This project aims to recreate the feel of the original Manaita-style experience for modern Minecraft: a progression-based crafting mod centered on unusually large crafting multipliers, fast resource growth, and intentionally exaggerated progression.

title: Build Your Campfire
description: A lightweight, vanilla friendly mod that changes the way campfires are built
body:
## Build Your Campfire: A Back to Basics Approach

 

Do you ever feel like crafting a campfire takes away from the immersion of survival? **Build Your Campfire** is a lightweight mod that injects a touch of wilderness realism into Minecraft by changing how you build your essential resting spot.

 

This mod allows you to build a campfire using the most basic materials, sticks and flint, without needing to use a crafting table for it! The vanilla crafting recipe for the campfire was also changed, in order to keep compatibility with other mods that uses campfires as crafting ingredients. Now, you need 3 large sticks at the bottom, a flint in the middle right and a charcoal/soul sand at the center of the recipe, depending on the campfire variant you want.  

 

#### **Features**

*   **Back to Basics Crafting:** Ditch the crafting table! Craft a **Large Stick** by simply combining two sticks in your inventory (shapeless recipe).
*   **Natural Campfire Building:** Right-click with the new large sticks in the ground to start building your campfire! Use four Large Sticks to create an unlit campfire.
*   **Light it Up:** Ignite your campfire the classic way with flint and steel or fire charges.
*   **Dual Flint Frenzy:** Feeling extra prepared? Light your campfire with flints in **both hands** for a true survivalist showmanship!
*   **Blue Flames:** Need a soul campfire? Just right-click the campfire build, **while not completed**, with a soul sand or soul soil and enjoy the blue flames.
*   **New Campfire Cooking Recipes:** New recipes like placing sticks in the campfire to create torches are added 

 

**This mod is perfect for players who:**

*   Enjoy a more realistic and immersive experience.
*   Want a more survival friendly approach to campfires.
*   Appreciate vanilla-friendly mod mechanics.

***

 

**❓ F.A.Q. ❓**

*   **Q: Is this mod compatible with other campfire mods?** A: This mod is designed to be lightweight and shouldn't conflict with other campfire mods that add functionality, but it may disable their crafting recipes.
*   **Q: Can I still craft a campfire the old way?** A: No, the vanilla recipe for the campfire will be disabled. A new crafting recipe using the new large sticks is added (both to the normal and the soul campfire variants) for modpack compatibility purposes.
*   **Q: May I use this mod in my modpack?** A: You are more then welcome to use this mod on your modpack! The only rule is that the download refers back to the CurseForge environment, no outside links are allowed for direct download.

***

Special thanks to stohun for helping me out with the models and textures for the 2.0 version  

**We hope you enjoy Build Your Campfire!**

# PokéNet

**PokéNet** is a Cobblemon side-mod that introduces a unique, Pokémon-powered storage network inspired by systems like Applied Energistics 2, Refined Storage, and Tom’s Storage. Instead of relying on traditional machines or energy systems, PokéNet uses Pokémon themselves to power and expand the network.

_This mod is still WIP so things will change this is a release for getting FEEDBACK_

## Features

- Players build a modular storage system using special PokéNet blocks. Each module can house a Pokémon, which becomes visible inside the block and actively contributes to the network. Depending on the Pokémon’s species, type, stats, and other attributes, different features of the storage network become unlocked or enhanced.

- Certain Pokémon enable entirely new capabilities, such as crafting terminals, PC access, item transfer through pipes, or wireless network access. Others improve the network by increasing storage capacity, speeding up item transfer, or enhancing crafting performance. Multiple compatible Pokémon can be installed across modules, allowing their bonuses to stack and scale the network as it grows.

- PokéNet encourages players to experiment with different Pokémon combinations to build powerful and specialized storage systems. Training stronger Pokémon or choosing the right species can significantly improve network performance, turning Pokémon into the heart of a fully automated logistics system.
